title: Device and Media Protection
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terminology of Device and Media Protection.
Apply device and media protection to a small synthetic example and identify evidence that supports the conclusion.
Identify a relevant limitation or failure mode and describe a safe defensive response.

content.intro: This lesson covers device and media protection in the Endpoint and Operating System Security track. It preserves the PDF's listed subtopics and develops a small, checkable defensive example. You will practice stating scope and assumptions, selecting relevant evidence, and describing what remains uncertain.
content.why_it_matters: Use documented baselines and synthetic alert examples; avoid changing a personal or production machine without approval and a rollback plan. The specific focus here is device and media protection; connect each subtopic to an observable check or a documented decision.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Device and Media Protection focuses on removable media policies; data loss prevention; disk encryption and recovery keys. Define the system or data in scope, the expected behavior, and the consequences if that behavior fails. Then select a proportionate control and identify evidence that can verify both the normal path and an important failure case.

items.text: For removable media policies, define the expected behavior, the system or data affected, and the relevant trust boundary. Record a safe verification step and one limitation rather than treating a successful demonstration as proof of complete security.

items.title: Disk Encryption and Recovery Keys
items.text: Cryptographic protection depends on a suitable standard algorithm, a secure mode or protocol, correct parameters, unpredictable values where required, and controlled key lifecycle. Prefer reviewed libraries and never design a new scheme for production.

content_blocks.title: Defensive example (synthetic data)
content_blocks.code:
endpoint = {"patch_state": "current", "disk_encryption": True, "local_admin_count": 1}
print("patch state:", endpoint["patch_state"])
print("disk encryption enabled:", endpoint["disk_encryption"])
print("review admin count:", endpoint["local_admin_count"])
content_blocks.expected_output:
patch state: current
disk encryption enabled: True
review admin count: 1
content_blocks.notes: This example uses synthetic values and has no network dependency. CodeLeaf displays it as instructional text; production does not execute arbitrary learner code.

content_blocks.title: Safety and verification
content_blocks.text: Endpoint defense combines secure configuration, least privilege, updates, protective controls, telemetry, and tested recovery. Before attempting any live security test, obtain explicit permission and verify that the target and method are within scope. When a secure isolated runner is not available, treat the code as a local/synthetic example and do not run arbitrary content on production infrastructure.

content_blocks.title: Run, verify, and reset
content_blocks.text: Review the python snippet as a local calculation. If you choose to run this example, use Python 3 and synthetic inputs in a disposable local environment; compare the displayed expected output with what you observe. If the result differs, check the copied inputs and runtime version, restore the synthetic input, and repeat. No scan, external request, or production change is needed.

content_blocks.text: Recap: Device and Media Protection focuses on removable media policies; data loss prevention; disk encryption and recovery keys. content.task: Create a concise, reviewable artifact demonstrating Device and Media Protection. Use synthetic data or a controlled local training environment only. Include the relevant syllabus subtopics (Removable Media Policies; Data Loss Prevention; Disk Encryption and Recovery Keys), state assumptions, show what evidence would support your conclusion, identify one failure mode, and recommend a defensive next step. Do not test systems outside written authorization.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use only a synthetic dataset, a disposable local lab, or an explicitly authorized system.
Include a clear scope/assumption statement and enough sanitized evidence for another learner to follow the reasoning.
Explain one limitation, edge case, or failure mode.
Recommend a proportionate defensive control and describe how to verify it safely.
hints: Write the expected behavior and test boundary before looking at a result.
Change one assumption at a time; compare results against the original synthetic case.
Record evidence and uncertainty separately, and select a proportionate protective action.
content.expected_output:
patch state: current
disk encryption enabled: True
review admin count: 1
troubleshooting: The example is illustrative and should be reviewed against current platform/version documentation before production use.
If an output differs, check the input and runtime version; do not broaden the activity to an unrelated system.
Use only fake data and remove all temporary local artifacts when the exercise is complete.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one observation as conclusive proof.
common_mistakes.why: Security telemetry and tests cover only the cases they were designed to observe.
common_mistakes.fix: Corroborate important claims and document coverage gaps.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing a target without confirming authorization.
common_mistakes.why: A technical ability to reach a system does not grant permission to assess it.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic input or a local lab; stop if the approved scope is unclear.

common_mistakes.problem: Skipping the version and context assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Security controls and protocol details vary across implementations and deployment models.
common_mistakes.fix: Record versions, configuration, expected output, and the source used for verification.

summary: Device and Media Protection is best understood within its defined scope and trust boundaries.
Use relevant evidence and test both an expected case and a meaningful failure case.
Record uncertainty and choose a proportionate, authorized defensive next step.
